newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sells majority stake in brewery firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sells majority stake in brewery firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state has sold 75 percent of Pyramids Breweries, also known as al-Ahram Beverages and Egypt's sole brewer, to a group based in the United States for 285 million pounds, investment banking sources said on Thursday.
The government said on Wednesday the state Holding Company for Housing, Cinema and Tourism had approved the deal but it did not name the buyer.
"It is the Luxor group, owned by Egyptians living in the United States," a source told Reuters.
The value of the deal, at 74 pounds a share, was between 12 and 13 percent higher than valuations by foreign consultants and the state's own auditing office.

The shares last traded on the Egyptian stock exchange at 66.50 pounds, 0.50 below the price at which the state sold 15 percent of the company in July. Company employees have taken the balance of 10 percent.
The firm made net after-tax profits of 42.980 million pounds in the financial year 1995/6, 35.8 percent up on 31.654 million in 1994/5, according to audited results. The year ends on June 30.
Turnover rose to 130.100 million pounds, 11.0 percent up on 117.185 million in the previous year, and profits before tax were 59.810 million, 31.7 percent up on 45.408 million.
